A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STaR research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Mixamo evaluations, ScanRet retargeting examples, component ablations, and a 21-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental and user-study results and adds shape-representation ablations and loss-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The final model retains the same encoders, spatial and temporal transformers, residual prediction, losses, and inference procedure. The whole-cloud explanation documents the existing method; STaR (Curv) is an additional weighting configuration, not a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Mixamo with the same seen/unseen character and motion scenarios, ScanRet human-motion examples, and the same user-study coverage. The added analyses vary model configurations and measure efficiency without introducing another dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces R2ET w/ Filter with R2ET†, explicitly described as a debugged version using balancing weights. Appendix I adds a timing comparison against R2ET's SDF loss and its limb-limb extension. Other benchmark and user-study comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 changes the curvature criterion from lower being better to closer to ground-truth curvature being better. It also evaluates STaR with greater smoothness weighting and introduces matched-vertex timing on an RTX 4090. Existing splits, sequence lengths, training budget, and metric formulas remain unchanged; the new smoothness weight is unspecified.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence with skeleton-only, DSR, combined-input, and joint-separated point-cloud comparisons in Appendix H/Table 6, plus comparative loss timing in Appendix I/Table 7. Table 1 adds a smoothness-weight configuration, while the earlier temporal-filter analysis disappears. Existing component, sampling-density, orientation, global-motion, and inference-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly describes the global-motion/height correlation as statistically nonsignificant, replacing v1's statement that no clear correlation was found. This is a limited statistical-reporting change: neither version specifies a test, p-value, repeated-run count, seed, or uncertainty interval, and the wording does not establish that additional analysis occurred.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SAN curvature from 32.65 to 8.16, reversing its smoothness ranking against final STaR at 10.66. Filtered R2ET's results are replaced by the distinct debugged variant, with curvature 7.87; new STaR (Curv) reports 8.70% penetration and 7.76 curvature. Final STaR and Tables 2–5 retain their numerical results. Table 6 adds representation comparisons, and Table 7 reports 16.32 seconds/iteration for STaR's loss versus 127.66 and 133.77 for the SDF alternatives.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations remain substantively unchanged. V2 corrects loss labels, including Lt to Ltc in Equation 3, without changing their formulas. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added; the curvature preference changes without changing its definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about sequence-based retargeting, dense shape representation, penetration constraints, and temporal consistency balancing semantics, geometry, and smoothness. The additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the post-filter interpretation with discussion of debugged R2ET and the smoothness–penetration tradeoff. Appendix H adds a rationale for preferring whole-cloud geometry over skeleton or joint-separated inputs. The conclusion removes the sparse-semantic-supervision limitation and the specific explanation of false contacts on larger characters.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-page link, RTX 4090 timing hardware, and an Andrena HPC acknowledgement. It clarifies nearest-neighbor lookup and whole-cloud encoding before the joint-channel MLP. Table 4 newly identifies its global-motion experiment as a preliminary model variant; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a changed experiment.

R1.justification: The same 20 cited works and core related-work discussion remain. Appendix H adds specific positioning against R2ET's skeleton bounding-box information and the spatially aligned, frame-wise approaches of references 19 and 20.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, rewrites the quantitative-results discussion, and condenses limitations. It adds acknowledgements and two appendix sections, moving Demo Videos from H to J. Most prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains skeletal-only/skinned method groupings, and Table 2 replaces descriptive variant names with component checkmarks. Tables 6–7 are added, curvature header symbols change, and Table 3 renames Motion Coherence to Motion Smoothness. Figures 1–9 retain their substantive content, with sizing and page-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: The reported debugged R2ET comparison and explicit smoothness–penetration tradeoff make Table 1 more informative. Tables 6–7 directly support representation and efficiency claims, and the code-page link improves access documentation. These benefits outweigh the removal of the sparse-supervision caveat, although missing debugging and tuning details limit the reproducibility gains.
